get verb

fetch, go and get

also fetch, go and get, go for, summon, send for (summon)

classical

Gell. 17.8.8: nōnne īs curriculō atque oleum petis?
Plin. NH 9.169: petere Brundisium ostreās (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 314

petō, petere, petīvī, petītum

verb, third conjugation

go for, fetch (a thing)

Of going somewhere for something (Lewis & Short). “Bring it here” is affer (bring).

Other words

  • arcessō (accersō), arcessere, arcessīvī, arcessītum — fetch, call (a person)

    verb, third conjugation · classical · Plaut. Men. 875: accersam medicum; Traupman 286

    Of making someone come (Lewis & Short): medicum arcessere, to fetch the doctor.

  • addūcō, addūcere, addūxī, adductum — fetch, bring (a person)

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Traupman 322

  • afferō (adferō), afferre, attulī, allātum — fetch, bring (a thing)

    verb · also used · classical · Traupman 322

Examples

  • verberō … nōnne īs curriculō atque oleum petis?

    You rascal … won’t you run and get some oil?Gell. 17.8.8

  • ībō atque accersam medicum jam quantum potest.

    I’ll go and fetch the doctor, as fast as I can.Plaut. Men. 875

  • ad sē vocāre

    to summon, call someone to oneselfTraupman 286

See also get, bring, fetch water, send, doctor.
